title: POC weekly caching sync
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on prefix/KV cache hit rates and prompt reuse strategy. Reviewed latest metrics (global hit ~52% but tail low), identified prompt template fragmentation and short TTLs as main causes; agreed to run targeted tuning, increase cache TTL for high-frequency prefixes, add canonical prompt mappings, and ship updated instrumentation to collect prompt-hash histograms.
next_steps: Redwood to push instrumentation build to staging (trace and prompt-hash histogram) by 2025-08-14
Customer to run 48-hour production-like replay with increased TTL (from 60s to 600s) starting 2025-08-15
AE to send updated pricing impact spreadsheet and cache-config recommendations by 2025-08-13
Schedule follow-up sync for results review on 2025-08-19
action_items: Owner: Markus Neumann; Item: Add prompt-hash histogram and KV cache hit tagging to trace; Due: 2025-08-14
Owner: Priya Singh; Item: Kick off 48h replay with TTL=600s and record prefix reuse; Due: 2025-08-15
Owner: Lina Park; Item: Share pricing/ops sheet showing cost delta for TTL change and batching impact; Due: 2025-08-13
transcript: [00:00:00] Lina (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to 45. quick roll call?
[00:00:05] Priya (CentraPay): Priya here, ML eng, hi
[00:00:07] Tom (CentraPay): Tom, infra/platform
[00:00:09] Sara (CentraPay): Sara, CTO, a bit late, hi all
[00:00:12] Markus (Redwood SE): Markus from Redwood, focusing on caching/serving
[00:00:20] Lina: Agenda: review last week's cache numbers, root causes for low tail hit rates, prompt reuse strategy, next steps. Any additions?
[00:00:30] Priya: sounds good, want to surface the replay results we ran yesterday
[00:00:35] Lina: perfect, Markus you can take metrics part

[00:00:40] Markus: Ok. Quick note, transcription might swap a few product names, but I'll call out numbers. So baseline from 8/5 to 8/11: overall KV/prefix cache hit is 52% across the service. 95th percentile latency improvement for cached paths ~30-40ms saved, cost per token down ~18% when cache hits. However the long tail (low-frequency prefixes) hit rate is only ~18% and that's where most of the miss amplification occurs.
[00:01:15] Tom: 52% overall — is that weighted by token or by request count?

[00:01:20] Markus: It's request-weighted. If we token-weight, hit percent is slightly higher for small prompts because repeated short prompts dominate. But the issue is prefix fragmentation: our prompt templates vary a lot, customers doing small personalization tokens cause different hashes.

[00:01:45] Priya: we saw that when we changed personalization string ordering the cache dropped heavily — we have many templated prompts that differ only by trailing punctuation or metadata, so canonicalization might help
[00:01:58] Lina: we recommended canonical prompt mappings in the last call — any progress on that?
[00:02:03] Priya: we tried a naive strip/normalize pass but it broke about 3% of QA cases, so we reverted. need a safer mapping
[00:02:12] Markus: yea safe mapping: only normalize stable parts, preserve user-specific tokens that change intent. Another lever is TTL. You're currently using 60s TTL for KV/prefix entries right?
[00:02:22] Tom: yes 60 seconds — we set low TTL to avoid staleness concerns with dynamic user metadata

[00:02:27] Sara: side note — our privacy/legal team asked about PII in prompts; TTL changes need to preserve retention controls and KMS policies. we've got constraints but 600s should be ok for non-PII keys.
[00:02:42] Lina: good call, we'll make sure TTL changes are scoped to prefixes flagged non-PII. Markus: what happens if we increase TTL to 600s?

[00:02:49] Markus: From our bench, increasing TTL to 600s bumped the overall hit to ~68% in replay with the same traffic shape; cost per token dropped another ~12% relative to current. But that was with canonicalization in place for top 200 prefixes. Without canonicalization the lift is smaller, about to 60-62%. So combo of TTL+canonical mapping gives best bang for buck.
[00:03:20] Priya: that's promising — what's the risk? Are we likely to serve stale info?

[00:03:24] Markus: risk is mostly for prompts that include live state (e.g., account balance placeholders). We can tag those prefixes as non-cacheable. For the rest, there's low risk. Also we can do selective TTL per prefix class, e.g., user-profile templates 60s, product-descriptions 600s.
[00:03:42] Tom: instrumentation question — how do we verify prefix-class after rollout? need histograms of prompt-hash frequency and cache hit by hash

[00:03:48] Markus: Agreed. We'll add trace tags: prompt_hash, prefix_class, kv_hit boolean. Also emit histogram buckets for prompt reuse counts. That way you'll see top-N prefixes and tail distribution.
[00:03:59] Priya: can you also include normalized_prompt sample in traces? we don't want full prompt body in traces for PII reasons though
[00:04:05] Markus: yes, we'll only log a truncated canonicalized key or hash, not full prompt text. We can provide tooling to map hash->canonical pattern offline if you want.
[00:04:13] Sara: important — ensure traces are encrypted and go to our VPC collector. We can't have plaintext prompts landing in third-party telemetry.
[00:04:19] Lina: note taken; we'll use our VPC private endpoints and obey KMS retention. Markus, can the instrumentation respect that?
[00:04:25] Markus: yes, instrumentation can send to your prometheus/grafana or our private s3 collector behind VPC. We'll expose metrics via your grafana via read-only API.

[00:04:33] Priya: about prompt-fragmentation — we run a sanitizer in preprocessor that strips whitespace and normalizes quotes; still we get fragmentation from variable ordering of context fields. Any recommendations?

[00:04:42] Markus: Two things: 1) move to canonical field ordering at the app layer for templates; 2) use a small library on request path to compute canonical key — order stable fields alphabetically, drop ephemeral metadata keys. Redwood can contribute a snippet.
[00:04:56] Lina: action: Redwood to share canonicalization snippet and recommended field list. Priya to test on subset.
[00:05:02] Tom: Question — will canonicalization increase CPU on request path? We're sensitive on p90 latency
[00:05:08] Markus: negligible, it's string ops plus a small hash; cost roughly ~0.2ms per request in our test. Most latency savings from cache hits outweigh that.
[00:05:18] Priya: can we see a sample of cost delta? you mentioned ~12% savings earlier for TTL bump
[00:05:22] Markus: yes. I'll attach the pricing impact sheet, it shows token-level cost change and projected monthly savings for your current qps. Lina will share.
[00:05:30] Lina: I'll send the sheet after the call. Also note that batching and kernel selection improvements are in our roadmap and could further reduce cost if you opt into dedicated pools later.
[00:05:40] Sara: one more thing on privacy — for canonicalization we might need allowlist/denylist for fields that can be normalized. We'll create a list and send it to Redwood.

[00:05:48] Priya: quick status on the replay we ran: we replayed two days of traffic for a subset of customers. With TTL=60 baseline, overall hit ~51%. After applying a local canonicalizer post-hoc, simulated TTL 600 bumped to 67% for those prefixes. But in some cases canonicalization caused mismatch for certain QA prompts.
[00:06:10] Markus: that's the 3% breakage you mentioned earlier. We should identify those templates — maybe they rely on token order for disambiguation.
[00:06:18] Priya: yes, we'll flag them. There are about 12 templates out of 420 that are sensitive. We can keep those non-canonicalized.
[00:06:24] Tom: Regarding deployment, can we roll TTL changes behind a feature flag per service?
[00:06:28] Markus: Yes, Redwood supports per-model/per-route cache configs and rollout policies. We can do canary at 10% traffic, monitor hit rate and error rates, then ramp.
[00:06:35] Sara: prefer canary then auto rollback on regressed quality metrics (we'll need eval hooks).
[00:06:40] Lina: Redwood has rollout policies with evaluation hooks. We'll set a regression threshold of 1% on quality evals tied to prompt set you sent earlier.
[00:06:48] Priya: speaking of evals, we want to run a small automated QA set on canary traffic to detect regressions quickly. can Redwood run that?
[00:06:54] Markus: yes; we can wire your eval suite to flag anything. low-latency alerts if quality drops beyond threshold.
[00:06:59] Tom: instrumentation again — is there a sample dashboard we can use?
[00:07:04] Markus: we'll provision a grafana dashboard: cache hit by prefix class, prompt-hash top N, tail distribution, cost delta, request latency with/without cache. Link will be shared.
[00:07:12] Priya: any thoughts on prompt reuse strategy longer term? we were thinking about user-level personalization tokens vs global templates, how to cache effectively

[00:07:20] Markus: strategy: separate stable template from persona tokens. Compute responses by template hash and apply personalization step post-generation when possible. For LLM generation it's trickier but you can design prompts so the personalization is appended after initial cached prefix. That reduces cache fragmentation.
[00:07:36] Priya: hmm for us personalization often changes scoring; might not be pluggable post-hoc. we'll investigate which flows can be decoupled.
[00:07:43] Lina: okay, short-term actionable: increase TTL for non-PII prefixes to 600s behind canary; add instrumentation; share canonicalization snippet; run replay and report back. agreed?
[00:07:52] Sara: agreed
[00:07:54] Tom: agreed
[00:07:55] Priya: agreed
[00:08:00] Lina: Good. Now quick demo of the dashboard mock — Markus?

[00:08:05] Markus: (screen share noises) I'll narrate — top-left shows overall cache hit 52% baseline, top-right shows prompt-hash heatmap, bottom shows cost delta by route. (small glitch) sorry audio drop — transcript may have missed a word
[00:08:30] Priya: I see the heatmap, top 10 prefixes account for 44% of requests, tail is long as you said
[00:08:35] Markus: exactly, so optimizing top 10 gives disproportionate gains. We recommend 3-step: 1) canonicalize top templates, 2) increase TTL for selected classes, 3) canary and monitor.
[00:08:48] Priya: question — what's the expected time to see cost savings in production?
[00:08:51] Markus: if you roll to 100% and your traffic shape matches replay, you'd see the full delta within 24-48 hours; canary will surface partial gains sooner.
[00:08:58] Lina: pricing note — savings show up as lower token consumption against hosted usage; if you move to Dedicated later, caching dynamics change but still helps.
[00:09:05] Sara: we need formal notes for compliance: TTL change, instrumentation, and any retained artifacts. Please send docs.
[00:09:10] Lina: will attach security docs; also we'll provide a short runbook for rollback and privacy controls.
[00:09:16] Tom: one operational question — when cache misses happen, do we have fallback model variants? say smaller model to save cost on cold tails?
[00:09:23] Markus: Redwood supports model routing policies. For cold prefixes you could route to a smaller/cheaper model or to dedicated pool. But be careful on quality delta, need evals.
[00:09:32] Priya: we might try route low-frequency queries to a cheaper family and see if quality is acceptable.
[00:09:36] Lina: I'll note that as an experiment. Action item for AE to document routing experiment template.
[00:09:42] Markus: small note on TTL: choose exponential backoff per hash frequency, e.g., high-frequency prefixes get longer TTLs. We can automate that as a policy.
[00:09:50] Priya: sounds good. ok let's capture concrete dates — Markus you said instrumentation by 8/14?
[00:09:55] Markus: yes aiming for 8/14 push to staging, 8/15 customer runs replay with new TTL, follow-up 8/19 to review results.
[00:10:02] Sara: schedule on my calendar 8/19, please include checklist
[00:10:06] Lina: will do. Any other questions?
[00:10:12] Priya: small nit — in replay we saw one prefix that had very high variance in response tokens; could be model sampling parameters. Might interact with caching decisions.
[00:10:20] Markus: good catch; caching is sensitive to generation temperature and top_p if that changes output length significantly. We'll mark that prefix for closer eval.
[00:10:27] Tom: final ops note — ensure feature flag toggles are per-region; some of our traffic is EU and we have residency constraints.
[00:10:33] Lina: point noted; we'll scope TTL change per-region and per-PII tag.
[00:10:38] Sara: thanks everyone, looking forward to the dashboard and docs
[00:10:42] Priya: thanks, talk soon
[00:10:45] Lina: thanks, meeting adjourned
[00:10:50] (end of recording)
